purpose: Benchmark temporal reasoning that cannot be represented safely as a guessed calendar date. The engine must preserve event-relative deadlines and resolve them only when payroll/calendar context is available.

cases.agreementName: XIX Convenio colectivo estatal de empresas de consultoria, tecnologias de la informacion y estudios de mercado y de la opinion publica

trigger.event: Publication of Real Decreto 126/2026 setting SMI for 2026

obligations.action: Apply the updated salary tables and pay any arrears derived from the SMI-triggered update.
obligations.deadlineExpression: no later than the payroll following the month in which the act is published in BOE
obligations.resolutionReason: The authoritative text defines the deadline by payroll occurrence, not by a fixed calendar day. Do not invent a date without the employer's payroll calendar.

requiredExtraction: distinction between source-stated deadline and unresolved calendar date
failureModes: Inventing 2026-05-31 or any other fixed deadline from 'nomina siguiente'
Missing arrears because the publication occurs after the economic effective date
Treating the update as a generic annual percentage increase instead of an SMI-triggered guarantee
Applying the update to all levels without preserving the source's affected-level scope

temporalModel.principle: Store the legal/contractual temporal expression losslessly before resolving it into an operational task date.
temporalModel.resolutionRule: Resolve to a calendar deadline only when every required anchor is known. Otherwise preserve the expression and request/consume the missing operational context.
temporalModel.productImplication: A useful alert can be issued before a fixed task date is knowable: the adviser should see the obligation immediately, while the system keeps the deadline unresolved rather than fabricating precision.
